proof_obligations.name: strong-maximum-principle
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: The annular exponential barrier has positive order-kappa-squared principal term; boundary comparison forces a nonzero derivative at a zero minimum.

proof_obligations.name: trace-kernel
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: The smooth elliptic trace operator has constants as its kernel on the connected compact manifold.

proof_obligations.name: adjoint-sign
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Opposite-sign adjoint bumps would produce a nonzero nonnegative right side in the trace range, contradicting the maximum principle.

proof_obligations.name: adjoint-positivity
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Subtract the global upper bound of the smooth adjoint zeroth coefficient and apply the minimum principle to exclude any zero.

proof_obligations.name: baseline-factor
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: p0/H is smooth positive, dd(chi0*h^(n-1))=0, and integral chi0*h^n=1.

proof_obligations.name: scalar-compatibility
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: The inverse of (v,c)->L_h v-c on zero dV-mean potentials has c=-integral g*chi0*h^n.

proof_obligations.name: factor-adjoint
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: The formal adjoint of A_h is (H/n)L_h; it has constant kernel and index zero.

proof_obligations.name: factor-inverse
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: A_h has zero-dV-integral range; restricting to integral eta*h^n=0 removes its chi0 kernel and gives a bounded inverse.

proof_obligations.name: norm-order
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: D controls both ddv and the endomorphism norm; fixed norms dominate pointwise operator norms and form a submultiplicative algebra.

proof_obligations.name: quadratic-remainder
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: The convergent log-det series gives Q=2*C_trace*D^2 and the stated quadratic bound on the radius1/(2D) ball.

proof_obligations.name: remainder-difference
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Telescoping matrix powers gives the stated Q*(norm v+norm w)*norm(v-w) Lipschitz bound.

proof_obligations.name: coefficient-perturbation
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Finite polynomial expansion of omega^(n-1), followed by two derivatives, gives the fixed C_A operator bound C2alpha to C0alpha.

proof_obligations.name: explicit-radius
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: r=min(1/(2D),1/(4KQ),m/(4G*C_A*D*C0)) and epsilon=r/(2K) are positive and contain no lower-mass constant.

proof_obligations.name: first-self-map
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: K*epsilon+K*Q*r^2<=3r/4 and2KQr<=1/2 on the complete product ball.

proof_obligations.name: metric-comparison
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Dr<=1/2 gives h/2<=omega<=3h/2; b=log V+c yields the exact unnormalized equation.

proof_obligations.name: smooth-bootstrap
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Differentiate the uniformly elliptic local log-det equation; Schauder improves each derivative from initial C4alpha. Taylor nonlinear regularity provides a matching scoped interface, not a fresh recursive proof-tree verification.

proof_obligations.name: factor-contraction
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Stokes puts every perturbation right side in Z0; kappa<=m/(4C0)<=1/4 gives an affine contraction on the complete normalized factor space.

proof_obligations.name: factor-bounds
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: The fixed point has norm eta<=2*kappa*C0<=m/2, hence m/2<=chi<=3*max chi0/2; elliptic regularity gives smoothness.

proof_obligations.name: factor-uniqueness
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Every normalized C2alpha factor solves the same fixed-point identity; uniqueness is over the full normalized affine space.

proof_obligations.name: normalization-Z
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Z=integral chi*h*omega^(n-1)=integral chi*omega^n by distributional Stokes; 2^(-(n-1))<=Z<=(3/2)^(n-1).

proof_obligations.name: current-test
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: T_F=(chi/Z)*omega^(n-1) is strictly positive, dd-closed and h-trace normalized.

proof_obligations.name: all-current-bound
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: For every positive normalized Gauduchon current S, integral omega*S=1, and matrix AMGM bounds Gamma_F(S) by exp(-b/n)*omega*S.

proof_obligations.name: attainment
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: The cofactor matrix of omega gives pointwise equality for T_F, so M(F)=exp(-b/n), and b=B0(F).

proof_obligations.name: equality-cases
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Zero integrated nonnegative deficit forces W^(1/2)P_S W^(1/2) scalar at trace-almost every point, including singular trace measures.

proof_obligations.name: singular-maximizer-regularity
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: An equality current is a nonnegative scalar distribution times omega^(n-1); its dd-equation is elliptic, hence the scalar is smooth.

proof_obligations.name: exact-current-uniqueness
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: The normalized full factor uniqueness and the trace condition identify every exact maximizing current with T_F. This is also consistent with the existing weak compact-duality theorem.

proof_obligations.name: probability-density
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Gamma_F(T_F)/M(F)=omega*T_F=(chi/Z)*omega^n; its density q has integral one.

proof_obligations.name: determinant-density
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: The smooth positive (n-1)-power root gives k=(chi/Z)*(omega^n/dV)^((n-1)/n), with q=exp(F/n)*k/M(F).

proof_obligations.name: exact-q-constant
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Combining chi/Z<=(3a/2)*2^(n-1) with volume<=(3/2)^n Hmax gives C_nu=3^(n+1)*a*Hmax/4.

proof_obligations.name: exact-k-constant
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: The same comparison with volume exponent(n-1)/n gives C_k=3^n*a*Hmax^((n-1)/n)/2.

proof_obligations.name: critical-exponent
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: q probability implies norm q in L^(n/(n-1))<=C_nu^(1/n); dV probability gives norm k<=C_k.

proof_obligations.name: adjoint-and-support-sign
proof_obligations.independent_reconstruction: Integration by parts annihilates L_omega against q dV; the maximizing-current/Jensen argument gives B0(G)<=B0(F)-integral(G-F)q dV.
